notable_absence.finding: 'Roles attribute — Select if you want the IdP to manage user roles. Works the same way the Groups attribute works.' explicitly offers a mechanism that BYPASSES Server's own user-group indirection entirely: unlike configure-ldap.md's mandatory group-mapping chain (LDAP group -> Server user-group -> role), SAML can assign roles DIRECTLY from an IdP attribute with no Server-side group object required at all. This is a real, page-stated structural difference between idp:ldap's and idp:saml's mapping mechanisms that this round's brief did not anticipate (it only flagged the LDAP-vs-Capella-SSO distinction) - flagging it for reconciliation as a second, intra-Server axis of variation worth its own note on idp:saml, separate from the idp:ldap-vs-sso:group-mapping distinction.

cross_product_finding: Confirms and extends the idp:ldap note (see configure-ldap.json's cross_product_finding): SAML's 'Roles attribute' mechanism, like LDAP's group mapping, resolves onto Server's own local role/group catalogue rather than Capella's management-plane capella-role:* catalogue - the same control-plane distinction idp:saml's existing promoted description already draws. Notably, SAML's own mapping is even MORE direct than LDAP's (no mandatory intermediate Server user-group object is required), making it, if anything, structurally closer to a naive reading of Capella's sso:group-mapping than LDAP's own three-hop mechanism is - despite both SAML and LDAP integrations resolving onto the SAME (Server-local) catalogue, unlike Capella's SSO. This is worth flagging precisely because it shows product-mechanism similarity (direct attribute-to-role assignment) does NOT imply catalogue/control-plane similarity - the two axes vary independently.
